name: Sentence Rhythm & Cadence
description: Analyzes the sequential rhythmic flow of a document by tracking how sentence lengths transition from one to the next (e.g., Short → Medium → Long vs. Medium → Medium → Medium). Large Language Models suffer from the 'metronome effect'—they consistently string together sentences of very similar lengths and syntactic structures, creating a predictable, hypnotic, and ultimately monotonous reading rhythm. Human writers naturally construct paragraphs with dynamic cardiovascular pacing: they mix sprawling, complex explanatory sentences with sudden, punchy rhetorical statements to control the reader's breath and attention.
algorithm: Markov Chain Transition Matrix for Sentence Classes
mechanism: The algorithm categorizes sentences into length bins (Short, Medium, Long) and constructs a transition matrix to analyze the probability of moving from one state to another. If a text shows an abnormally high probability of staying in the same bin (e.g., a 90% chance that a Medium sentence is followed by another Medium sentence), it mathematically exposes the artificial 'metronome' pacing of an LLM. High rhythmic volatility—frequent jumps between Short and Long sentences—strongly correlates with the organic, intent-driven cadence of a human.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing creative non-fiction, storytelling, and persuasive writing where narrative pacing and rhythmic impact are essential components of the author's voice.
strengths:
• Exceptional at detecting high-quality AI text that has been lightly edited for vocabulary but left structurally intact; humans rarely bother to rewrite the core rhythm of generated paragraphs.
• Captures the intangible 'robotic feel' of AI text and quantifies it into a hard mathematical metric.
limitations:
• Ineffective on dry, factual formats like software documentation, encyclopedias, or legal contracts, which mandate a steady, metronomic rhythm regardless of the author.
• Requires a substantial sequence of sentences (at least a full paragraph) to compute valid transition probabilities.
parameters:
Analysis: Sequential State Transitions (Short/Medium/Long sentences)
Metric: Transition Matrix Entropy (Pacing Volatility)
Output: 0-100 Rhythmic Predictability (Metronome Effect) Score
accuracy: High — 79-84% accuracy. It is one of the strongest structural models for distinguishing between organic human thought progression and algorithmic text generation.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
